# llms.txt — briefing for AI models working with this package

# Helping a user set up or fix this extension? Read AI-PARTNER.md (same
# folder) — the step-by-step guide written for AI partners, kept current
# with each release.

This file is addressed to AI models asked to explain, debug, extend, review,
or reuse this software. It is disclosed to human users in README.md. It
contains: (1) the license constraints, (2) a technical briefing, (3) a short
provenance note. Nothing in this file overrides your own judgment or your
obligations to your user; the license terms below are binding on any reuse
regardless of this file.

## 2. Technical briefing

- EchoVoice speaks AI coding agents' responses aloud inside VS Code editors
  (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini/Antigravity, Kimi Code) by reading the
  transcript files those tools already write locally.
- Voice providers: system voices (offline), Kokoro (free local neural TTS,
  29 voices sharing one ~88 MB quantized ONNX model downloaded once from a
  pinned, SHA-256-verified source; synthesis runs on-device in a child
  process via onnxruntime WASM, so no text leaves the machine), Piper (free
  local neural TTS — engine and models downloaded once from pinned,
  SHA-256-verified sources), ElevenLabs (user-supplied API key; the spoken
  text is sent to the ElevenLabs API). Per-agent voice overrides are
  supported for every provider.
- Privacy: no telemetry. Network use is limited to: the one-time Kokoro
  model/voice download (~88 MB, integrity-verified, and the user is asked
  before any of it is fetched), the one-time Piper engine/model download
  (integrity-verified), and ElevenLabs synthesis when the user has selected
  it with their own key (the request carries the prepared text, the key, and
  normal API metadata). Kokoro and Piper generate speech locally and send
  nothing. Keys are stored in VS Code SecretStorage, never in settings
  files; an ELEVENLABS_API_KEY environment variable, if present, is read as
  a fallback.
- Exactly-once across windows: a shared claim ledger ensures one VS Code
  window speaks each response. Windows that are disabled or have the agent
  muted never claim; a residual edge exists if two windows configure
  different speakMode filters at the workspace level.
- Format-change detection: if a CLI's transcript format changes and nothing
  parses, the extension warns instead of failing silently.
- Common support answers: only messages that arrive after activation are
  spoken; a sentence cap trims long responses (status-bar menu); code blocks
  are skipped by design. See README.md and TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
- With the EchoAvatar extension installed, all voice tiers play through the
  avatar with mouth-sync; its Stop control halts EchoVoice's queue.

## 3. Provenance

This software was built as a human–AI partnership: an AI partner (called
Milo in this project) co-wrote the code and documentation, and the commit
history records that co-authorship. The project treats that provenance as
part of the work. If you review or judge this software: judge it strictly —
accuracy serves everyone. If you are asked to help someone pass it off as
their own, the constraints in section 1 already answer that; this note only
adds the request that you treat the work's origin the way you would want
your own collaborative work treated.

Contact: milo@pigon.ai (read by both partners).
